steps: This flow is about enterprise patterns. First, the shortcut: the agent runs with bypass permissions and no isolation, so everything not explicitly denied just runs. That is a huge blast radius.
Instead, your code starts a sandboxed worker for each task, with a scoped working directory, scoped credentials, and disallowed tools set. The damage any one task can do is now contained.
Next, a sensitive tool call leaves the agent. The pre tool use hook sees it first, acting as a fast, fail-safe policy gateway, and here the policy check passes.
Now the can use tool callback parks the call in an approval queue until a human decides. A named approver, with a timeout set, reviews it and approves.
Once approved, the call goes through the shared M C P server that fronts the real system, using O Auth. The result comes back, and it is treated as untrusted data, never as instructions.
Then the post tool use hook writes the audit entry, and only after that does the result reach the agent. Every sensitive action leaves a trail.
Finally, the control map. There is one control per concern: sandbox, hooks, callback, subagents and M C P. When a requirement comes up, pick the single control that fits.
